questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The choices of academic courses, the examination forms, and the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Both on their website but also from the coordinators and the student administration.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance of locations of classrooms, register for courses and exams, to make and get a student card e.g.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy since there were many providers in Lund city but also around e.g., in Malmö. But you need to be careful since I heard stories of cheaters that provide housing to students which are fake.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You are more far away from the student-life, so you need to engage more than if you lived on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy. I was already registered in advance by application, so to be honest, I did not need to do a lot on my own when I arrived.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I chose the courses in advance through application, and there were no problems hereon, so I didn't need to take further action. The application itself was easy to fill out too. The administration sent a link through e-mail, and all the important information was given.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could easily write to the student administration if any questions would appear.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. No problems. I got the courses that I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to register and apply for courses as an exchange student at Lund University. So just go for it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied. The way that they teach, and their learning strategy is completely different than my home university, and it was very learning.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was equal to my home university. So, the level was high as you can expect from being a master student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was the same style as University of Copenhagen where you have a professor teaching in front of class, but furthermore you had group work, group presentations, oral presentation of your planning exam paper, feedback on other's oral exam, your written exam paper and you are also evaluated on your performance during lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 'EU Law and Policy in AI, Big Data and Digitalization' and 'Mergers and Acquisitions in the EU'.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The same courses as I had: 'EU Law and Policy in AI, Big Data and Digitalization' and 'Mergers and Acquisitions in the EU'. Very interesting courses, a good way of teaching and the exam form itself was very different and learning.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: To register for a student nation was 310 SKK per semester. It is not a lot compared to what you can get from the nation in relation to programmes and social life, but I didn't knew.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Nothing was more expensive than I expected. It was more and less what I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of student associations (so-called nations), gyms, sports clubs and a lot of student life. Easy to be involved.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many. Both cultural, athletic, and social activities. Both from student associations, organizations etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participate to the social student life, enjoy a fika (coffee and cake) with your fellow students. Go to nations for lunch (cheap and homemade lunch for students), partying, cosy times and the many nations makes a lot of programmes for all the students as bike rides, theme days or parties, games, trips etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Many students travelled to nearby cities or e.g., went to nature parks, hiking, bicycling trips in Sweden.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everybody was welcoming and polite.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Since you are having lectures with local students, I recommend taking the initiative to make social programmes as I did. A fika (coffee and cake) after or before class or invite your fellow students out for a drink or food or a trip somewhere. It worked very successful for me.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That local students wanted to socialize with international students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and kindness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be social and enjoy as many social events as possible that you can. Remember a bicycle. Lund has a bicycle culture, and it is hard to get around without.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Take the initiative to make social programmes with your fellow students. Many of the other students are in the same position as you, and they want to socialize. 
Remember an umbrella and a bike. It is a northern climate after all.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of meeting so many smart and sweet students from all over the world with different histories and cultures. They outcome from the academic courses and exams was also extremely rewarding. Besides, the different teaching methods were definitely rewarding too.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular besides be prepared to be challenged with a high-level English from your professors and your fellow students.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Lund University is an amazing university that host so many international students. It was a pure pleasure and even though Sweden seems similar to Denmark, it was a completely new and different academic experience for me. I would always recommend Lund University for an exchange, and I will never forget my time as a student there. The city itself has an amazing student vibe and simply is so cosy for students to go around or to sit in the many cafées or parks, and you can definitely feel that you are amongst a lot of international students. If you consider an exchange there, go to the city as a one-day trip before and feel the atmosphere. You will fall in love.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
